resources.string: PairFree talks to your earbuds over Bluetooth, and Android asks you to allow that. Later it may ask for two more things, both only for its status notification and both optional: to show notifications, and to link PairFree to your earbuds so the notification can appear when they connect.
Without Bluetooth access the app cannot reach your earbuds.
Pick your earbuds. Close the official app (PeatsAudio, Soundcore) first: only one app can hold the controls.
No supported earbuds paired. Pair them in the Bluetooth settings first.
No account. No internet. Nothing leaves this phone.
Could not reach the controls of %1$s. Close the official app (PeatsAudio, Soundcore) if it is open, check the earbuds are connected for audio, then try again.
Bluetooth access is turned off for PairFree.

The settings of %1$s need Android 17 on this phone. Before Android 17, Android\'s Bluetooth opens their channel only on Pixels with Android 16 QPR3 and on OnePlus, OPPO and realme phones with Android 16.
%1$s did not answer on its Bluetooth address. PairFree can look for it nearby if you allow it to find nearby devices; it never uses that for your location.
Turn LDAC off to use this
Your phone picks the codec. On Samsung phones, also check that LDAC is on for these earbuds in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings.
Turn on LDAC on the phone too

The earbuds now offer LDAC, but your phone picks the codec it plays. On Samsung phones, open Bluetooth settings, tap the gear next to these earbuds and check that LDAC is on there. Other phones may have a similar switch, such as HD audio. Android does not let PairFree see which codec the phone uses.
On these earbuds LDAC and two devices take turns: turning one off turns the other on. The earbuds reconnect each time, which takes a few seconds.
PairFree does not change the equalizer on this model yet: nothing has confirmed the EQ it would send. A recording of the Soundcore app setting it, sent from the button below, adds it for everyone.

PairFree does not support the equalizer for these earbuds yet. If you want to change EQ settings, you can contribute to the project by tapping the button below. It takes a few minutes with the official PeatsAudio app.
Reading the EQ from the earbuds…
These earbuds cannot report their EQ, and this phone has not set one on them yet. Pick a profile or move a band to set it.
Presets are fixed curves. Pick New or one of your own profiles to set bands one by one.
Presets are fixed curves. Pick Stock, New or one of your own profiles to set bands one by one.
Equalizer curve. Pick a band below to change it.
Added the profile from the file.
That file is not a PairFree profile for these earbuds.
The profile is removed from this phone. The earbuds keep the sound they have now.
The earbuds report their EQ, so this shows what they hold, whichever app set it.
The earbuds report which preset they use, but not a custom curve, and they forget a custom curve when they turn off. PairFree keeps the last one it set and sends it again each time it connects.
The earbuds apply this preset themselves. Samsung does not publish its curve.
0 dB on every band is the earbuds\' own tuning. The earbuds cannot report their EQ, so each time PairFree connects it puts back the one this phone last set, as the official app does.
These are for when both earbuds are in. Each earbud keeps its own for when it is used alone; they show here while only one is in.
Only one earbud is in, so these are its actions for when it is used alone. The ones for both earbuds show here once both are in.
When off, the earbuds ignore taps and holds.
A sound in the earbuds when they take a tap.
Every tap and hold goes back to what the earbuds came with.
These earbuds did not report any touch controls.
Blends noise cancelling and transparency to suit your surroundings.
How much noise Adaptive Audio lets through: 0 lets in the most, 100 the least.
Turns the media down and lets voices in when you start speaking.
Adjusts the media volume to your surroundings.
Lets pressing and holding the stem switch noise control off too.
Turns the music down and lets voices through, for a quick talk.
Lets in a little ambient sound, so the ears do not feel blocked while noise cancelling is off.
Makes voices stand out in ambient sound.
Adds one more ambient sound level.
Allows noise cancelling and ambient sound with only one earbud in.
When you start talking, the earbuds switch to ambient sound and lower the media volume.
Double tap the edge for volume
Double tap the edge of the left earbud for volume down, of the right for volume up.
Hear your own voice more clearly on calls.
Calls play through the earbuds while they are in your ears, and through the phone when they are not.
Switch between your Samsung devices without pairing again.
Wake the voice assistant by voice
The earbuds beep loudly: take them out of your ears first. Mute one to hear the other.
Take the earbuds out of your ears first. The beep is loud.
Check that each ear tip seals well. A good seal gives fuller bass and better noise cancelling.
Put both earbuds in your ears and stay still somewhere quiet. The earbuds play a short sound and check how well each ear tip seals. It takes about 10 seconds.
Noise control turns off for the test and back on afterwards.
For an earbud with a poor fit, push it in a little further and twist it slightly so the tip seals, then test again. If it still does not fit, try a larger ear tip.
No result came back. Check that both earbuds are connected and in your ears, then try again.
Plays a series of sounds for about 30 seconds to push water out of the speakers, for example after rain or a workout. Take the earbuds out of your ears first.
Draining. The earbuds stop by themselves after about 30 seconds.
Uses Bluetooth LE Audio where the phone supports it. The earbuds restart to switch and reconnect by themselves.

PairFree learns what a model can do, and its equalizer, from what its official app (PeatsAudio, Soundcore or Galaxy Wearable) reads from the earbuds and sends to them. Android can log that, and one recording per model is enough to add it for everyone.
Turn on Developer options: in Settings, open About phone and tap Build number seven times. On Samsung it is under About phone, Software information.
In Settings, Developer options, set Bluetooth HCI snoop log to Enabled (not Filtered). Then turn Bluetooth off and on.

Open the official app for these earbuds with them connected. Open each of its screens once, so it reads every setting. Then change each setting you want PairFree to learn, one at a time and a few seconds apart, and note what you changed. Do not come back to PairFree yet. If PairFree\'s status notification shows for these earbuds, set it to None on the Device tab first: while it shows, the official app cannot connect.
On SOUNDPEATS earbuds, also run PeatsAudio\'s fit test if it has one, and on its EQ screen tap SOUNDPEATS Classic and every other preset once, a few seconds apart.
Back in Developer options, tap Take bug report, then Full report.
It takes several minutes, and Android shows nothing while it works. Wait for the notification that says it is ready.
When the notification says the bug report is ready, tap it and share it to PairFree. If you miss the notification, tap Choose a bug report below, open the menu and pick Bug reports to find it.

PairFree shows what it found. On SOUNDPEATS earbuds, name the EQ curves in the order you tapped them. Then send the report, and write in it what you changed in the official app. If PairFree is connected to the same earbuds, its own device report goes in too.
Afterwards, set Bluetooth HCI snoop log back to Disabled and delete the bug report. It holds a lot of personal data.
Reading the bug report. This can take a minute.

PairFree reads the bug report only on this phone. From the Bluetooth log inside it, it reads only the messages exchanged with earbuds of the brands PairFree supports, and skips everything else. The report shows only messages PairFree knows, with the earbuds\' address and serial number masked; of the others it shows little more than their number and size. It does not keep the file. Nothing is sent to any server until you send the report yourself, which opens GitHub in your browser. PairFree has no internet access at all: its app info in Android lists no network permission.
This bug report has no Bluetooth log. Set Bluetooth HCI snoop log to Enabled, turn Bluetooth off and on, use the official app again, then take a new bug report.

The Bluetooth log in this bug report has nothing from earbuds PairFree supports. Check that the snoop log was set to Enabled, not Filtered, and Bluetooth turned off and on, before you used the official app.
That file is not a bug report.

resources.string: All of them are presets PairFree already knows, named for you.
From %1$s, when you opened this recording.
Not in the log. Turning Bluetooth off and on before opening PeatsAudio records it. The report is still useful without it.
A model PairFree does not know yet (%1$s)
PairFree\'s own device report for these earbuds goes in too.
To add PairFree\'s own device report as well, connect these earbuds in PairFree before sending.
No EQ curves in this recording. The settings are still worth sending.
At its end the report has a place to write what you changed in the official app, in order. That tells which message is which setting.
Name at least one curve to send the report.

Nothing has left this phone yet. Send on GitHub copies the report and opens a new issue with it filled in, in your browser. It is sent only when you submit the issue there. If the issue is empty, paste the report into it.
Copied. If the new issue on GitHub is empty, paste the report into it, then submit it.
Pause when an earbud is taken out
Sony\'s single noise cancelling setting, made for wind. Only while noise cancelling is on.
Pauses the music and lets in ambient sound when you start speaking.
Sony\'s upscaling for compressed music. On means automatic.
The earbuds report the preset or curve they hold, whichever app set it. They apply their presets themselves, so no curve is drawn for those. Clear Bass is below.
These Sony earbuds have not listed an equalizer, or have not answered yet.
Bose\'s steps, as its own app counts them.
PairFree cannot set the equalizer of AirPods and Beats yet.
PairFree cannot set the equalizer of JBL headphones and earbuds yet. JBL\'s app sends a whole curve of filters, and PairFree does not send what it has not checked.
Bose earbuds and headphones have a tone control rather than an equalizer of bands by frequency. Where the model has one, it is below.
The battery and buttons for noise control in the notification shade while these earbuds are connected. PairFree keeps their connection open meanwhile, so their official app cannot connect.
Google\'s Fast Pair notification shows their battery. PairFree shows none.
PairFree shows no notification for these earbuds.

Google shows its own battery notification for these earbuds too, and PairFree cannot hide it. To see only one, turn Google\'s off in Google Play services\' notification settings. That covers every Fast Pair device on this phone.
Android does not let PairFree show notifications yet.

To show it when the earbuds connect while PairFree is closed, Android asks once to link PairFree to these earbuds. Its prompt says a linked app can sync information such as a caller\'s name; PairFree uses the link only to start this notification.
Show it when the earbuds connect?

Android starts PairFree\'s notification when these earbuds connect, with PairFree closed, only once PairFree is linked to them. Android\'s prompt that follows says a linked app can sync information such as a caller\'s name. PairFree uses the link only to start this notification, and it still has no internet access.
The battery and noise control of the connected earbuds.
Noise control: %1$s. Tap for the next mode.
Copied. Paste it into a device report issue on the project page to help support these earbuds.
Every setting on the earbuds goes back to how it left the factory. They may also forget this phone; then pair them again in the Bluetooth settings.
Adapt noise cancelling to the surroundings
